A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same detector-robustness and style-aware paraphrasing study despite changes in title and organization. All 22 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and appendices, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original detector evaluations across Reddit, Amazon, and Blogs, style-transfer comparisons, and ablations in Sections 2 and 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds detector controls, latency and semantic-drift measurements, cross-model evaluations, and essay experiments.

M1.justification: The supervised training, DPO, and iterative SBERT-ranked paraphrasing procedure remain unchanged. Appendix L adds a limited inference adaptation for essays: split into paragraphs, paraphrase each independently, and merge them. Newly disclosed backbone and iteration details do not establish changes to the existing core method.

E1.justification: V3 extends the retained short-text domains and Reddit style-transfer task to GEDE essays, including whole-essay and paragraph-based scenarios in Appendix L. Appendix K also adds detection when support examples come from a different generator, expanding the input conditions beyond the original support-setting evaluation.

E2.justification: V3 adds SemDetect, a semantic detector using the same 100 support examples as StyleDetect, to Table 1. Appendix J evaluates Qwen3-14B as a zero-shot and few-shot detector. The established attack baselines and main nine-detector suite remain; Detector-Guided DPO renames the existing Mistral-7B-DPO-FastDetectGPT baseline.

E3.justification: The main detection metric changes from AUROC(10), restricted to false-positive rates up to 10%, to AUROC(1), restricted to 1%; Appendix C additionally reports full AUROC. New protocols cover newer generators, prompted LLM detection, mismatched support generators, latency measurement, and 250 GEDE essays evaluated using one to five paragraphs. Newly disclosed settings for retained experiments do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained exemplar-count, paraphrase-count, and DPO ablations, v3 adds semantic drift across inference iterations (Table 5), token-rank and perplexity analysis of existing examples (Table 2), cross-model support robustness (Appendix K), and whole-essay versus paragraph-wise rewriting (Appendix L). These test additional mechanisms and failure conditions.

E5.justification: V2 reports edit-distance and semantic-similarity point estimates; v3 Tables 3 and 6 add standard deviations, also reported for the new iteration analysis. Neither version reports seed-based uncertainty, confidence intervals, or formal significance tests. The added dispersion statistics do not establish additional training runs.

E6.justification: V3 adds substantial detector, latency, semantic-drift, newer-generator, cross-model, and essay results. For example, Table 17 reports AUROC(1) of 0.7387 for Chunk & Merge versus 1.0000 for Full Essay at five paragraphs. Table 3 changes semantic-similarity means from 0.90 to 0.91 for Prompting and 0.86 to 0.85 for Ours. Table 1's optimization averages match v2's values but replace the per-model breakdown. Detection curves under the revised metric are not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The training-data and conditioning equations retain their mathematical substance. The new preliminaries explain existing style representations using mapping notation without introducing a substantive mathematical result, assumption, or proof. The AUROC cutoff revision changes evaluation rather than theoretical reasoning.

C1.justification: V3 broadens the foregrounded robustness claim from detector-guided optimization to optimization, prompting, and paraphrasing attacks, and explicitly lists multi-document detectability among its contributions. The central claims about style-aware paraphrasing, single-document evasion, and recovering detection with more samples were already present in v2.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly acknowledges StyleDetect's support-information advantage and interprets the SemDetect control as evidence for stylistic robustness. It adds discussion of TinyStyler's statistical-artifact tradeoff, shared cross-model fingerprints, segmentation's relationship to training lengths, and practical conditions for obtaining multiple documents. The original exemplar-access, computational-cost, and semantic-drift limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 identifies the RoBERTa-base preference detector, discloses generation temperature and top-p, three-epoch baseline DPO, three inference iterations, and latency hardware/framework details. It clarifies Reddit-only training and length controls. The resource statement changes from a promised anonymous release to reported public availability of datasets, implementations, and checkpoints; actual availability cannot be verified from the PDFs. These are substantial documentation and access-information additions.

R1.justification: V3 adds Gehring and Paaßen's GEDE work and a passage distinguishing the proposed paraphraser from DIPPER and earlier authorship-style methods, including more explicit novelty assertions about machine-text rewriting and DPO. Most related work is retained; numerous reference changes update publication metadata for existing citations.

P1.justification: V3 changes the title and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, robustness argument, and conclusion. It adds a preliminaries section, moves inference into the method section, reorders baselines and datasets, and relocates the unchanged style-transfer evaluation from v2 Section 5.3 to Appendix D. The narrative and organization are substantially revised.

P2.justification: V3 adopts a two-column main text and references, removes v2's introductory UMAP/cartoon figure, redesigns Table 1, and adds perplexity and token coloring to Table 2. It consolidates eight appendix plots into two multi-panel figures and adds several tables and a full-AUROC figure. Retained visualizations are resized and relocated.

improvement.justification: The matched-exemplar SemDetect control and cross-model test strengthen v2's attribution of robustness to style. Essay, latency, and semantic-drift analyses also improve assessment of practical tradeoffs. These gains are tempered by lost per-model detail and new reporting errors: Appendix J calls OUTFOX a detector although the reported comparison treats it as an attack, and Appendix I claims reductions at every sample size despite Table 14 showing ties. V3 offers better-controlled evidence, but these weaknesses limit the overall quality gain.
